Definition: from G2596 and G2961; to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate:--exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome.
BiblicalUsage: The princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over their people, and Jesus says it shall not be so among you, because whoever will be great must be a minister. Peter tells the elders not to be lords over God's heritage but examples to the flock, and the possessed man in Ephesus overcame the seven sons of Sceva by the same power turned evil. Dominion is either service or tyranny, and the difference is the heart.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the kingdom turns dominion upside down, because the greatest is the servant of all. I hold that any leader who lords it over God's people has forgotten whose they are, and I want no part of that kind of power.
